questions.q: What is the article mainly about?
options: The Fed's revised 2027 schedule, which drops the October vote and December meeting
The Fed's plan to raise interest rates at its October 2027 meeting
Warsh's confirmation as chairman and his first months running the Fed
The history of the dot plot and why Warsh decided to bring it back
questions.explain: It describes the revised schedule under Warsh's plan to meet less often.

questions.q: What will the Oct. 26-27 meeting be dedicated to?
options: A vote on the near-term policy outlook
questions.explain: It will be dedicated to the discussion of broad monetary policy strategy.

questions.q: When will the Fed next vote on rates after November 2027?
questions.explain: Without a December meeting, the next vote is Jan. 25-26, 2028.

questions.q: By 2028, how many rate-setting meetings will the Fed hold under the plan?
questions.explain: Six rate-setting meetings and two strategy-focused meetings.

questions.q: What is one possible downside of meeting less often?
options: More impromptu meetings, typically reserved for crises
Higher borrowing costs for households after each missed meeting
Longer news conferences that crowd out strategic discussion
A larger dot plot with more projections from each official
questions.explain: Fewer chances to adjust policy may force impromptu meetings, usually reserved for crises.
